summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent epigastric pain and vomiting, previously attributed to pancreatitis but now under question, was admitted for symptom management and diagnostic evaluation. Initial workup revealed only a mildly elevated lipase and normal imaging, casting doubt on pancreatitis. A HIDA scan showed normal gallbladder ejection fraction, ruling out biliary dyskinesia. The clinical team, in consultation with her gastroenterologist, concluded her symptoms were likely due to an intestinal motility disorder with visceral hypersensitivity. Her diet was advanced from NPO to clear liquids, then soft, and finally regular diet as symptoms improved. Pain and nausea were controlled with oral medications by discharge. She was discharged home with PRN Dilaudid and Prochlorperazine, continuation of psychiatric medications, and referral to a motility specialist for outpatient follow-up. Her mental health conditions remained stable throughout the admission.
